items.title: Headlines for November 04, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## Voters Deliver Stunning Rebuke of Trump with Democrats Regaining Control of Congress Nov 04, 2026 In a stunning repudiation of President Trump and his MAGA movement, Democrats regained control of the House and the Senate in Tuesday’s midterm elections. Democrats have picked up at least seven Senate seats, winning races in Texas, Maine, Ohio, South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa and Kansas, as well as winning in Michigan. The Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska remain too close to call. In the House, Democrats have won at least 231 seats, with more races still to be decided. Only twice in the last half-century has control of both chambers changed hands in the same election. Democrats also clinched a majority of governorships. ## Historic Night in Texas as Democrats Win Senate Seat and Governorship Nov 04, 2026 In Texas, Democrats have shattered more than three decades of Republican dominance, winning races for U.S. Senate, governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general and even railroad commissioner. And Democrats are poised to possibly take control of the Texas House of Representatives for the first time since 2003. James Talarico will be the first Democrat to represent Texas in the U.S. Senate since Lloyd Bentsen left in 1993. Talarico spoke at a victory rally Tuesday night after defeating Trump-backed MAGA Republican Ken Paxton. ... Meanwhile, Texas Republican Governor Greg Abbott has lost his bid for a fourth term. Democratic state Representative Gina Hinojosa defeated Abbott by nearly 700,000 votes. She becomes Texas’s first-ever Latina governor. ... ## Progressive Michigan Democrat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed Elected First Muslim Senator Nov 04, 2026 In Michigan, progressive Democrat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed has defeated Republican former Congressman Mike Rogers in the race for an open Senate seat. El-Sayed campaigned on a platform of Medicare for All, ending military aid to Israel, and getting money out of politics. He becomes the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. Throughout the campaign, El-Sayed faced racist, Islamophobic and vitriolic attacks by top Republicans, led by President Trump, who mocked El-Sayed’s name and Muslim faith. Throughout his campaign, El-Sayed called for an end to U.S. military support for Israel, saying Michiganders’ tax dollars would be better spent at home. ... ## Democrat Annie Andrews Wins South Carolina Senate Seat in a Stunning Upset Nov 04, 2026 In South Carolina, Democrat Annie Andrews has defeated Republican Senator Darline Graham by about 50,000 votes, out of 2 million cast. It’s a stunning upset in a state that Trump won by 18 points two years ago. Graham was appointed to fill the remainder of the term of her brother, the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, who died in July. Senator-elect Annie Andrews is a pediatrician from Charleston who opposes cuts to Medicaid and supports a public health insurance option. ... ## Mississippi’s Senate Race Remains Too Close to Call Mississippi’s Senate race remains too close to call. With just a few thousand outstanding provisional ballots yet to be counted, Democrat Scott Colom leads Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith by just 43 votes out of nearly a million cast. ... ## Democrat Deb Haaland Becomes First Native American Female Governor in U.S. History In New Mexico, Democrat Deb Haaland has won the governor’s race. Haaland is a member of the Laguna Pueblo and will become the first Native American woman governor in U.S. history. ... ## Midterm Elections Result in Several Historic Firsts In California, Mexican American Democrat Xavier Becerra was elected to succeed Gavin Newsom as governor. Along with Gina Hinojosa in Texas, the country’s two most populous states will be led by Latino governors starting next year, both areas that were once part of Mexico. In Georgia, former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms has defeated billionaire Republican healthcare executive Rick Jackson. Bottoms becomes the first Black woman ever elected governor in the United States. ... ## Trump Announces U.S. to Stop Providing Israel $4 Billion in Annual Military Aid Early on Election Day Tuesday, President Trump said that the U.S. will stop providing Israel with roughly $4 billion in annual military aid starting in 2027, though the U.S. will continue to sell Israel weapons. items.title: US services sector activity cools slightly in October; inflation remains elevated By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 4 (Reuters) - US services sector growth slowed marginally in October amid a moderation in new orders, but supply chains remained strained, keeping prices for inputs elevated. The Institute for Supply Management said on Wednesday its nonmanufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index dipped to 54.5 last month from 54.9 in September. A reading above 50 indicates growth in the services sector, which accounts for more than two-thirds of US economic activity. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the PMI little changed at 54.8. The PMI suggested the economy started the fourth quarter on solid footing, though economists expect a slowdown in activity, with consumer spending expected to pull back after back-to-back quarters of robust growth. Spending is seen in part curbed by high inflation, which is eroding household purchasing power. Income at the disposal of households, after adjusting for inflation and taxes, fell in September after being unchanged in August. The saving rate is at a four-year low of 3.8%. The survey’s measure of new orders received by services businesses decreased to 55.9 last month from 59.8 in September. Delivery performance by suppliers deteriorated further against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Israel war with Iran and tariffs on imports. The Middle East conflict, now in its ninth month, has boosted energy prices and caused shortages of commodities that are shipped through the Strait of Hormuz. The survey’s measure of supplier deliveries jumped to 56.7 from 53.2 in September. A reading above 50 indicates slower deliveries. Deliveries have slowed for 23 consecutive months, keeping input prices high. The survey’s measure of prices paid by businesses for inputs eased to a still-high 73.0 last month from 74.0 in September. The ISM on Monday reported a slight moderation in prices paid for inputs by manufacturers in October. Economists expect inflation to continue to run above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target into 2027. The Fed last Wednesday left its benchmark overnight interest rate within the 3.75%-4.00% range while acknowledging that inflation "remains elevated." Economists expect the US central bank to raise borrowing costs in December. The ISM survey showed a marginal increase in services sector employment, aligning with economists’ expectations for moderate growth in nonfarm payrolls in October. The survey’s measure of services employment rose to 51.4 from 50.1 in September.

items.title: Entertainment News Live Updates Today (November 4, 2026): Shraddha Kapoor Opens Up On Not Signing Films After Stree 2 | Ramayana Premiere Alia Bhatt Ranbir Kapoor | Tiger Shroff Attack Case Update - Filmibeat
items.excerpt: One of the biggest talking points is the theatrical release of the Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash-starrer Ramayana Part 1 on November 5. Last night, the makers hosted a special premiere for the film, which was attended by the team and many well-known celebrities. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, the mythological drama is just one day away from hitting the silver screens and has been creating a huge buzz. ... Playback singer Kanika Kapoor, known for songs such as Baby Doll, Lovely and Da Da Dasse, has announced her separation from husband Gautam Hathiramani after four years of marriage. The 48-year-old musician shared the news in a post on her Instagram Stories, saying that the separation was decided after much thought and consideration. "Dear friends and family, after much thought and consideration, my husband and I are going our separate ways. I am grateful for the time we shared and wish him well for the future," Kanika said. "I sincerely ask for kindness and respect for our privacy as we move forward," she added. Sreeleela has boarded the cast of superstar Rajinikanth's next feature film "Dharman", the makers announced on Wednesday. Backed by Kamal Haasan's Raaj Kamal Films International, the film will be directed by filmmaker Ashwath Marimuthu of "Oh My Kadavule" and "Dragon" fame. Nov 04, 2026, 1:09 pm IST Former James Bond star Pierce Brosnan is backing fellow actor Callum Turner to play the iconic role in the upcoming James Bond movie. Brosnan played the British spy in four films, from 1995's GoldenEye to 2002's Die Another Day. Expressing his admiration for all the actors who are in contention to play the iconic British spy, Brosnan singled out Turner, with whom he worked on 2017 romantic drama The Only Living Boy in New York. Nov 04, 2026, 12:16 pm IST Jason Statham is reuniting with British filmmaker Guy Ritchie for their seventh film, Dogfight, which is set in the London criminal underworld. Announced by Netflix, the movie is described as a "stylish revenge actioner". Other plot details are not available for now, Variety reported. Production is due to commence in early 2027, with filming taking place in the UK. Ritchie will write, direct and produce the film that will be produced by Black Bear Pictures, Ritchie's own Toff Guy Films and Statham's Punch Palace Productions. Nov 04, 2026, 9:49 am IST ## Why Shraddha Kapoor Didn't Sign Films After Stree 2? Shraddha Kapoor has spoken about a career decision she took following the huge success of Stree 2. The actress, who is currently preparing for her upcoming film Eetha, recently interacted with fans through an Instagram Q&A session. During the session, a fan asked her what advice she would give young girls about making career choices. Responding to the question on Tuesday, Shraddha revealed that she turned down several film offers, including lucrative projects, after Stree 2 because she wanted to wait for the right story. She said, "I would share about myself. After Stree 2, I was offered a lot of films and money as well, but I had decided that until I get that perfect story, I won't sign anything. My heart said that I will have to keep that patience, and I did that." Nov 04, 2026, 9:45 am IST

items.title: ‘The Hunger Games’ Goes 3D, Brad Pitt’s Cliff Booth Returns, and Rob Lowe Looks Back: Hollywood Movie News for November 4 - Manny the Movie Guy
items.excerpt: ### ‘THE HUNGER GAMES’ ENTERS A NEW DIMENSION The upcoming prequel The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will receive a 3D theatrical release through a new partnership between Lionsgate and Meta. According to a November 3 report from People, the collaboration will also make the film available in 3D on Meta’s forthcoming VR glasses after its theatrical run. The movie opens November 20. Director Francis Lawrence worked with visual-effects company DNEG on the conversion, intended to immerse audiences in the experience of a young Haymitch Abernathy, portrayed by Joseph Zada. The story takes place 24 years before the original Hunger Games and follows the brutal 50th Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell. The cast includes Ralph Fiennes, Jesse Plemons, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin, Maya Hawke and Mckenna Grace. ... ### ROB LOWE REVISITS HIS RISE, FALL AND REINVENTION Rob Lowe is opening up about his extraordinary Hollywood journey in the new Netflix documentary Rob Lowe: The Outsider, directed by Chris Smith. Entertainment Weekly debuted the documentary’s trailer on November 3, ahead of its November 24 premiere. The film revisits Lowe’s rise through The Outsiders and St. Elmo’s Fire, his personal controversies, his recovery from addiction and his eventual reinvention through television. Demi Moore and Gwyneth Paltrow appear, while Lowe’s wife, Sheryl Berkoff, discusses the difficult years behind his public persona. ... Brad Pitt’s return as Cliff Booth in The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is attracting attention for an unusual reason: very few people have seen the finished movie. The David Fincher-directed project, a follow-up to Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, is scheduled for November 25. A November 4 Page Six report says only the opening 17 minutes were shown at AFI Fest, with Academy screenings planned later this month.

items.title: Movie News: 4th November 2026
items.excerpt: Wild Horse Nine opens in the UK: Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine opens in UK and Irish cinemas today, via Searchlight, two days ahead of its US release on Friday. ... Statham and Ritchie reunite: Jason Statham is reuniting with Guy Ritchie for Dogfight, a Netflix revenge thriller set in London’s criminal underworld (so a real divergence then for both men!). ... Blumhouse Atomic: Jason Blum’s Blumhouse and James Wan’s Atomic Monster, which merged in 2024, have unveiled their new corporate name, Blumhouse Atomic, which must have taken them AGES to come up with! The two will, however, continue to trade as separate production labels. The combined company’s films have taken more than $2.5 billion worldwide against production budgets of less than $330 million, and in 2026 alone it has taken $1.3 billion, thanks to Curry Barker’s Obsession ($520 million worldwide) and Kane Parsons’ Backrooms ($400 million), both of which feature in our special ‘Flickering Breadcrumbs’ Top 10 Horror Films podcast. Next up is The Exorcist: Martyrs, and Wan is returning to the Saw franchise as producer. The American Film Market, continued: Several stars have joined Rebecca Miller’s Moonsong: A Life in Seven Verses, which stars Julianne Moore and Elle Fanning, and follows the writer Margaret Wise Brown in 1930s New York as she discovers her gift for children’s stories. Josh Hartnett, Emma Thompson, Sally Hawkins and Danny Huston are among the new cast members. Meanwhile, the Moroccan-Belgian superhero film Atoman has secured a North American release from Disrupt Entertainment, which plans to roll it out on at least 100 screens, ahead of an international sales push at the AFM.
